# Build DayQ Clothing

Build clothing as physical, localized, server-authoritative equipment that extends existing DayQ systems. Never create a parallel item, inventory, crafting, combat, contamination, movement, spawning, economy, journal, migration, or persistence owner.

Read both references completely before acting:

- [FULL_SKILL.md](references/FULL_SKILL.md) for the complete clothing contract.
- [INTEGRATION.md](references/INTEGRATION.md) for current ownership, schemas, evidence, and decision gates.

## Required workflow

1. Inspect current definitions, inventory transactions, equipment, crafting, survival, contamination, combat, armor, traversal, exoskeleton/mech, loot, AI, economy, persistence, rendering, tests, and technical budgets.
2. Classify the request by garment category, body regions, layer occupancy, material panels, fit, pockets/attachments, localized condition zones, environment channels, spawn route, and repair families.
3. Preserve localized garment damage as authoritative instance state. Allow aggregate replication only as a reversible projection.
4. Express definitions and operations through versioned schemas and data. Conserve mass and provenance through construction, cleaning, repair, replacement, and salvage.
5. Route visual production through `$build-dayq-systemic-asset-factory`; use a dedicated character/cloth pipeline when img2threejs cannot represent cloth, bodies, hidden geometry, or skeletal requirements.
6. Route runtime work through `$dayq-unreal-mcp-production-validation`. Require compilation, PIE or dedicated-server/client evidence, localized damage, inventory atomicity, persistence, restart, migration, visual, performance, and regression proof.
7. Update the no-skip ledger with `specified`, `implemented`, `testing`, `passed`, `failed`, or `blocked`. Never convert detailed prose into runtime acceptance.

## Locked decision

Localized garment damage is approved. A damaged knee, sole, seam, zipper, pocket, seal, plate pocket, strap, or exoskeleton interface changes only functions routed through that zone. Returning to global-only garment condition requires explicit user approval.

## Product gates still requiring explicit approval

Ask before adopting granular body measurements/body-shape restrictions, large rendering-cost increases from modular visuals, major clothing-care routine burden, changed regional scarcity, irreversible maximum-condition loss, or substantial armor/movement/stealth/climbing/exoskeleton rebalance. Present the prior assumption, proposal, consequences, evidence, recommendation, and reversible alternative.

## Required output

Deliver the affected contracts and data, ownership/dependency changes, exploit analysis, migrations, tests, evidence, unresolved gates, ledger update, and acceptance status. Use `blocked` when the Visual Studio toolchain, live Unreal MCP, PIE, representative content, multiplayer route, or performance evidence is unavailable.
